newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chubais tells miners new Russian govt will pay up.
newsitem.headline: Chubais tells miners new Russian govt will pay up.

text.p: Russia's new economy supremo, First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais, pledged on Friday to pay off the government's entire debt to pensioners and state employees by the end of the year, Itar-Tass news agency said.

"Now, as never before, we have a chance to turn the situation around in favour of the Russian people," it quoted Chubais, who is also finance minister, as saying in Siberia, where he attended the national coalminers' trade union congress.
"There is little left to do -- to push out the rest of the pensions and wages, get rid of delays. By December 30 we will pay off our salary debts to public sector workers."
At the end of February, Russian workers were owed 50 trillion roubles ($8.8 billion) in back wages, of which 10 trillion was owed by the state, hit by low tax collection.

Chubais was also quoted as saying in the Siberian city of Kemerovo that the government would pay all pensions due for January to March on schedule and pay off all backlogs in pensions before the end of June.
Chubais, 41, is the leading figure of a reform-minded new cabinet line-up under Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.

The new government was formed this week at the insistence of President Boris Yeltsin with a mandate to end the economic crisis and salvage free market reforms from the grip of an unwholesome mixture of graft, bureaucracy and organised crime.
In the short term, the government is also anxious to defuse public discontent ahead of a day of strikes and protests planned for March 27 across the country.

The chairman of Rosugleprofsoyuz, the national coalminers' union whose members work for the state coal monopoly Rosugol, told the congress that the miners were the worst affected by the web of non-payment gripping the economy.
The miners were owed some 2.7 trillion roubles ($475 million), Vitaly Budko said, calling on Chubais and the government to help.
Chubais said the young new team, including his fellow First Deputy Premier Boris Nemtsov, 37, was ready for action.
"We will take responsibility on ourselves," he said. "And if the Russian people put their trust in us for a little while, then today's very severe problems will be solved."

Labour leaders have softened their demands for government changes ahead of the March 27 protests following the cabinet reshuffle. But millions of unpaid workers and pensioners will have little patience if Chubais does not make progress quickly in paying the state's debts.

As a token of commitment locally, Tass said Chubais announced that the finance ministry had transferred 170 billion roubles to the Kuzbass coalmining region around Kemerovo on Friday to pay off debts on wages to public employees.
Total public sector wage arrears in the region were 500 billion roubles at the beginning of the year, Tass said.
